doc.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007

title: Listening habits, live music and Gene Harris
summary: She rarely listens at home, prefers live music, and regrets never seeing Gene Harris before he died.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Do you spend a lot of time listening? I mean when you’re at home and you’ve got a day off, are you a person who deliberately goes and puts on music as you do your —

Never as I’m doing anything. I can’t listen to music when I drive, it’s really dangerous. I’ve tried. And I can’t do both things. I’m not good — I don’t like background music at © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

all. But sometimes I will — I don’t listen to music like I used to before I became so involved in it. I mean I really just don’t. But I do, like at festivals I get to hear other people and sometimes I’ll go out and hear other people. My life right now, I have people at home I take care of. My mother-in-law lives with me and my mother is close by. And so I don’t go out as much as I did or will in the future sometime. I mean I certainly plan to spend more time listening to other people. But I love hearing live music. I mean listening to records is too pale by comparison. I mean to me it’s a person — music where it’s not nearly as good live is better than terrific canned music, and I don’t know why that is. I couldn’t tell you in a million years. And I do listen to people like Charles Brown or you know, I listen to all kinds of people. But when I heard him live, that really got in. It’s just different.
There’s that Big Bill Broonzy moment all over again.

Yeah. Oh absolutely. And you know I never got to see him live. Never. But he was live on the radio. You know? It was almost. And there are a lot of people I regret. I mean there’s this jazz piano player I heard on the radio once when I shouldn’t have been listening to the radio. A guy named Gene Harris. And I thought wow, that’s really great. I’m going to go see him. So I wrote his record company and I said could you tell me where he’s going to be? Would you put me on his mailing list. I’ve got all these frequent flier miles, I’m going to come hear him sometime. And it didn’t work out and it didn’t work out, and I kept thinking well next month, next month. And he died. Just very unexpectedly, suddenly. You know you’ve just got to go see them while you can, ‘cause—
You never know, and you never regret it.
